comparison: Both evaluate the awake ULM methodology (C5, C26-C37) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on methodological validation with surgical procedures and habituation protocols. Peer review emphasizes the experimental setting is 'very well described' and methodology is 'masterfully combined.' Both agree the approach is feasible and well-executed, though peer review includes additional claims about animal subjects (C138-C144).

Overlap on pupillary monitoring claims (C6, C34-C37). OpenEval groups this with broader methodological validation as SUPPORTED. Peer review separately evaluates pupillary monitoring as SUPPORTED, noting it's standard practice with no concerns raised. Both agree on the validity of this approach.

Both address MB count normalization method (C38-C47) and evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative evidence from Figure 2 showing stabilization at 5 million MBs. Peer review acknowledges 'quantitative information on their protocol' regarding MB requirements. Both accept this methodological innovation without concerns.

Both address anesthesia-induced vascular changes (C7, C48-C50, C78-C80). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with comprehensive imaging data. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with editor noting 'data supporting these findings are solid' but Reviewer 1 challenging statistical testing ('Why impose wrong statistics?') and Reviewer 2 noting variability may be similar to longitudinal changes. Significant disagreement on statistical rigor.

Partial overlap on differential arteriovenous responses (C9, C51-C57, C89-C92). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with statistically significant findings. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN for broader claims, questioning whether discrepancies reflect true biological differences or imaging limitations in pial vessels. OpenEval more confident in the mechanistic interpretation.

Both address differential arteriovenous effects (C9, C89-C92). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED emphasizing quantified differential responses. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 questioning whether observed differences reflect true vessel behavior or inadequate ULM quantification of pial vessels. Disagreement on data reliability underlying mechanistic claims.

Both address regional differences in anesthesia effects (C8, C58-C64). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with ROI-based analyses across brain regions. Peer review rates broader anesthesia findings as UNCERTAIN due to statistical concerns and variability issues. Disagreement on robustness of regional quantification.

Both evaluate longitudinal consistency claims (C10-C11, C65-C74, C102, C115). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED emphasizing TOST equivalence testing and smaller variations than anesthesia effects. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 noting 'longitudinal imaging seems to show a certain variability close to the order of magnitude observed under anesthesia,' contradicting the claim of clear separation. Significant disagreement on magnitude of longitudinal stability.

Both address technical advantages of awake ULM (C83-C84, C96, and C94-C95). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on demonstrated capabilities. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 acknowledging the 'masterfully combined' methods answer 'long-running' questions. Both agree on unique technical contributions.

Perfect overlap on study limitations acknowledgment (C99-C101). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate characterization given sample sizes. Peer review quotes Reviewer 1's concern about statistics but accepts the limitation is acknowledged. Both agree authors appropriately identify constraints, though peer review questions why statistics are used at all if study is exploratory.

Perfect overlap on motion correction limitations (C103-C106). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes thoughtful self-critique with relevant citations. Peer review accepts this acknowledged limitation without dispute. Both agree the limitation is appropriately identified and discussed.

Perfect overlap on residual isoflurane effects (C107-C114). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting magnitude not quantified and solutions speculative. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, accepting the transparent discussion of limitations. Disagreement on whether unquantified effects warrant uncertainty versus acceptance as acknowledged limitation.

Perfect overlap on motion artifacts (C118-C125). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes evidence from supplementary figure and appropriately speculative solutions. Peer review notes Reviewer 2 'calls for further caution' regarding motion, accepting authors' acknowledgment. Both agree this limitation is appropriately discussed.

Perfect overlap on literature context (C75-C77, C85-C88, C93). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive citations and accurate representation of field knowledge. Peer review acknowledges consistency with prior literature on isoflurane effects. Both agree the work aligns with existing research.

Overlap on comparative advantages over other modalities (C94-C95). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes accurate characterization of other techniques' limitations. Peer review acknowledges the combined methods answer long-standing questions. Both agree on unique positioning versus optical imaging and fMRI.
